passage: Prize-day rehearsal was in ten minutes, and the hall was full of drums and chairs scraping. Parul Ma'am snapped, "Vasudha, stop talking! You are ruining this," though it was the boy behind her who had been talking. Vasudha's ears burned. She had always thought Parul Ma'am was the fairest teacher. She said nothing through the whole practice. Afterwards, when the hall emptied, Vasudha walked up and said, "Ma'am, I felt bad when you said it was me. It was not." Parul Ma'am paused, then said, "I was rushed and I got it wrong. I am sorry."

qa.q: How much time was left before the prize-day rehearsal in the passage?
qa.a: There were ten minutes left before the rehearsal.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling when Parul Ma'am blamed her?
qa.a: She was shocked and hurt, since her ears burned and she had thought Parul Ma'am was the fairest teacher.

qa.q: What did Vasudha do well by waiting until the hall emptied?
qa.a: She spoke politely and privately about how she felt, which gave the teacher a chance to admit the mistake without being embarrassed. 🙂

qa.q: How might Parul Ma'am have seen the situation while rushing?
qa.a: She was under time pressure in a noisy hall and probably reacted without looking carefully, then recognised her error when Vasudha spoke up.

grounding: A child is shocked when her favourite teacher is unfair, then politely tells her how she felt without cutting her off.
